findings.title: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser row exists
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (a user may have no topic_users row for the topic — e.g. notifications driven by category/mailing-list settings, a row that was never created because of the `rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` swallow in `TopicUser.change`, or simply a user who types/visits the unsubscribe URL for a topic they never opened). The very next line calls `tu.notification_level`, raising `NoMethodError: undefined method for nil`, which surfaces as a 500 for a link that users click directly from email. The action needs to create/handle the missing record (e.g. via `TopicUser.change`) instead of assuming one exists.

findings.title: Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping, so the mute can be silently undone
findings.body: The new action mutates `notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` directly instead of going through `TopicUser.change`. Two consequences: (1) `notifications_changed_at` / `notifications_reason_id` are not set, and `TopicUser#update_last_read` only auto-tracks a topic `when tu.notifications_reason_id is null` — so after unsubscribing, the next visit to the topic will auto-bump the user back to `tracking`, undoing the unsubscribe; (2) no `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", notification_level_change: ...)` is sent, so other open browser tabs keep showing the stale notification level.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe exposed as an unauthenticated-looking GET (CSRF / link prefetch)
findings.body: `unsubscribe` is reachable via `GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and changes the user's notification level, while `check_xhr` is skipped. Rails CSRF protection does not apply to GET, so any third-party page can mute a logged-in user's topics with ``, and mail clients / corporate link scanners / prefetchers that fetch links in email bodies will mute topics without the user ever clicking. A mutating endpoint should require a POST/PUT (or a one-time signed key as the digest unsubscribe does), with the GET URL only rendering a confirmation page.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, breaking other callers
findings.body: The `unsubscribe_link` string gained a mandatory `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation, but it is rendered from `Email::MessageBuilder#body` / `#html_part` for every caller that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` was updated to supply `unsubscribe_url`; any other core mailer, job or plugin that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without it will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and fail to send the email (the spec change in `message_builder_spec.rb` had to add the param for exactly this reason). Give `unsubscribe_url` a default in `MessageBuilder#initialize` (or guard the per-topic sentence) so the option stays backwards compatible.

findings.title: Client route shows the unsubscribe confirmation without performing any unsubscribe
findings.body: The Ember `topicUnsubscribe` route only loads the topic view; the actual notification-level change happens server-side in `TopicsController#unsubscribe` during the initial HTML request. Any client-side transition to `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` (an in-app link, or browser back/forward handled by the SPA without a full page load) will render "You will stop receiving notifications for …" while nothing was changed on the server, misleading the user. The route should issue the unsubscribe request itself (or the page should reflect the level returned by the server).

findings.title: Confirmation text claims notifications stop even when the level is only lowered to 'regular'
findings.body: `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` always says "You will stop receiving notifications for <title>", but the server toggles: a user at `watching`/`tracking` is moved to `regular` (which still emails on replies to their posts, mentions and quotes) and only a second click sets `muted`. So the majority of users who click the email link are told notifications have stopped while they will still receive some. The message should reflect the resulting notification level.

findings.title: No specs for the new unsubscribe endpoint
findings.body: The PR adds a new state-changing controller action, route and `Topic#unsubscribe_url`, but no controller/request spec was added. The untested branches include: missing `TopicUser` row (currently a 500), the watching→regular vs regular→muted toggle, the slug-mismatch 301 redirect, the not-logged-in path, and that the JSON/HTML responses render. Without tests the toggle semantics and the nil case can regress silently.
